tools.name: fractal_version
tools.desc: The extension version and edition, the DuckDB version it is running in, and this MCP server's version.

tools.name: fractal_config_get
tools.desc: Reads back one configuration key of this DuckDB server: the reasoning plugin path, the chat and embedding endpoints, the model names, the think mode, the response mode or the enterprise library. The key names are the short ones the docs use (http_url, http_model, http_embed_url, ...); the environment variable behind each key is named in the docs too. The provider token is a secret and is never read back through any tool. Reading a key is not a write, so FSQL_MCP_CONFIG_WRITES does not restrict it.

params.name: key
params.desc: The configuration key to read: reasoning_plugin, http_url, http_model, http_embed_url, http_embed_model, http_think, http_think_provider, http_native_url, http_num_ctx, http_response_mode, http_allow_plaintext, http_token, enterprise_lib, enterprise_require_signature, ledger_retention, agent_use_index, agent_index_min_rows, agent_context_row_bytes, text_to_sql_allowed_statements or text_to_sql_use_review. http_token is refused: it is a secret.

tools.name: fractal_config_keys
tools.desc: Every configuration key the extension knows, as {name, type, session_overridable}: string, path, int, bool or enum (agent_use_index is an enum: off, on, auto). Lets a caller discover the keys instead of hard-coding them; every key is changed with fractal_config_set.

tools.name: fractal_config_set
tools.desc: Sets one configuration key of this DuckDB server (the DuckDB column's wrapper over fractal_config_set(key, value)): the reasoning plugin path, the chat and embedding endpoints, the model names, the think mode, the response mode or the enterprise library. The configuration is the environment the extension reads, so the new value is in force from the next call on. FSQL_MCP_CONFIG_WRITES decides what may be written: off refuses every key, safe (the default) allows the model names and the think mode only, and all allows every key. destructiveHint-flagged: repointing an endpoint silently redirects every subsequent reasoning and embedding call, and the enterprise key changes the tier that is loaded.

params.name: key
params.desc: The configuration key to write: reasoning_plugin, http_url, http_model, http_embed_url, http_embed_model, http_think, http_think_provider, http_native_url, http_num_ctx, http_response_mode, http_allow_plaintext (on or off), http_token, enterprise_lib, enterprise_require_signature (on only: turning the signature requirement off is an operator setting), ledger_retention (fade or exact), agent_use_index (off, on or auto: the retrieval and nearest-row agents search through a fractal_index), agent_index_min_rows (auto: the smallest table searched through an index), agent_context_row_bytes (the longest text cell passed to the model), text_to_sql_allowed_statements (select or select_insert_update) or text_to_sql_use_review (on or off). A key this build does not know is refused.

params.name: value
params.desc: The value to set. An empty value unsets the key, which is how a setting is turned off again.

params.name: allow_secrets
params.desc: Must be true to write an enterprise-posture key (enterprise_lib, ledger_retention): an explicit operator intent, never a default. A client UI that honours annotations prompts a human first for it.

tools.name: fractal_configure_reasoning
tools.desc: Configures the reasoning and embedding provider in one call: the chat endpoint (provider_url), the embeddings endpoint (embed_url), the chat model (model), the embedding model (embed_model) and the reasoning effort (think_mode). The DuckDB column's wrapper over fractal_config_set on this server's configuration: the change is in force from the next call on. FSQL_MCP_CONFIG_WRITES decides what may be written, and a call that names a key the switch refuses changes nothing at all. It never touches the provider token or the enterprise key: the token belongs in the server's environment. destructiveHint-flagged: repointing the provider URL silently redirects every subsequent reasoning call.

params.name: provider_url
params.desc: The chat endpoint (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/chat/completions for ollama, or an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions).

params.name: embed_url
params.desc: The embeddings endpoint (e.g. .../v1/embeddings); a distinct path from the chat one.

params.name: model
params.desc: The chat model name (e.g. gpt-oss:20b, gpt-4o-mini).

params.name: embed_model
params.desc: The embedding model name (e.g. nomic-embed-text); never reuse a chat model here.

params.name: think_mode
params.desc: The reasoning effort for hybrid-thinker models: unset or 'none' (the model default), 'off', or any provider-verbatim value (low/medium/high/...).

params.name: allow_plaintext
params.desc: Allow plaintext http:// endpoints (needed for local Ollama).

tools.name: fractal_agent_allocate
tools.desc: Cardinality-constrained portfolio optimisation, then a written rationale. Returns the allocation, its Sharpe ratio and the rationale (or the computed half plus reasoning_step_failed).

params.name: cov
params.desc: The n x n covariance matrix, flat row-major (nested rows are accepted).

params.name: cardinality
params.desc: At most this many assets carry weight (1 to n).

params.name: context
params.desc: Optional JSON object handed to the reasoner as context.

tools.name: fractal_agent_anomaly_triage
tools.desc: Drift on one entity's metric series read from a table, then a model-written triage summary. Returns threat_score, anomaly_type and triage_summary.

params.name: filter_col
params.desc: Column to restrict the cohort on (needs filter_val).

params.name: filter_val
params.desc: Keep rows whose filter_col equals this.

params.name: baseline_window
params.desc: Baseline window (16 or more); the series needs baseline_window + 16 samples.

tools.name: fractal_agent_data_analyst
tools.desc: Natural-language question over your tables: the model writes SQL, the engine validates and runs it, and the model analyses the rows.

params.name: table_names
params.desc: Tables to scope to (list of names).

params.name: max_retries
params.desc: Attempts the engine may make to correct a rejected statement.

params.name: context
params.desc: Optional JSON object handed to the reasoner as context.

tools.name: fractal_agent_detect_loop
tools.ret: STRUCT(agent_id VARCHAR, dfa_exponent DOUBLE, is_loop_detected BOOLEAN)
tools.desc: SimHash + Brent cycle-detection safety monitor for an agent's own behavior. A loop is flagged when EITHER signal fires; only the FIRST closed cycle is reported. Returns {agent_id, dfa_exponent, is_loop_detected[, cycle_len, at_index]}. GOTCHA: encode scalar states one-hot, not 1-dim, or a same-signed scalar log false-positives as looping.

tools.name: fractal_agent_detour_classify
tools.desc: Classify a vehicle detour: nearest fleet peer by route change plus the box-counting complexity of its GPS trace, with a written verdict.

params.name: gps_trace
params.desc: The flattened GPS trace, boxcount_dim values per point.

params.name: id_col
params.desc: The column to report as the id of each row (default id).

tools.name: fractal_agent_diverse_portfolios
tools.desc: Enterprise: several mutually different near-optimal portfolios (sharpe) or the return-versus-risk front (pareto), with a written comparison.

params.name: cov
params.desc: The n x n covariance matrix, flat row-major (nested rows are accepted).

params.name: cardinality
params.desc: At most this many assets carry weight (1 to n).

params.name: overlap_threshold
params.desc: How much two portfolios may share (0 to 1).

params.name: quality_frac
params.desc: How close to the best Sharpe a candidate must be (above 0, at most 1).

params.name: context
params.desc: Optional JSON object handed to the reasoner as context.

tools.name: fractal_agent_feedback_audit
tools.desc: Self-contained Diversify health-check cycle, NO LLM step: enable repulsion, warm the D_q window, report negative feedback on the top result, read back diagnostics, then SELF-DISABLE (a complete audit cycle). Returns {diversity_quotient, explanation}.

params.name: warmup_table
params.desc: Table whose first rows warm the session.

tools.name: fractal_agent_network_coverage_alert
tools.desc: Sensor-grid coverage: morphological dimension and lacunarity of the point cloud plus drift in the telemetry, then an alert.

params.name: point_cloud
params.desc: The flattened sensor coordinates, boxcount_dim values per point.

params.name: context
params.desc: Optional JSON object handed to the reasoner as context.

tools.name: fractal_agent_outlier_intercept
tools.desc: Intercept a proposed state that is too close to a known-bad one. Returns intercepted, the nearest distance and a reason.

params.name: metric
params.desc: cosine compares shape, l2 compares magnitude too.

tools.name: fractal_agent_patient_deterioration_triage
tools.desc: Cohort search plus the drift from baseline to current, then a written triage.

params.name: cohort_doc_ids
params.desc: Optional: restrict the cohort to these row ids.

params.name: id_col
params.desc: The column to report as the id of each row (default id).

tools.name: fractal_agent_plan_explore
tools.desc: Embed a seed state and branch it into the nearest strategies (rows). Needs an embedding provider.

params.name: initial_state
params.desc: State label (text, not a raw vector).

tools.name: fractal_agent_rebalance_sibling
tools.desc: Optimise a portfolio, find the most similar past allocation by weight change, and explain the rebalance.

params.name: cov
params.desc: The n x n covariance matrix, flat row-major (nested rows are accepted).

params.name: cardinality
params.desc: At most this many assets carry weight (1 to n).

params.name: alloc_emb_col
params.desc: Column holding the weight vector of each allocation.

params.name: id_col
params.desc: The column to report as the id of each row (default id).

params.name: context
params.desc: Optional JSON object handed to the reasoner as context.

tools.name: fractal_agent_recall_hybrid
tools.desc: Pure retrieval, no model: the nearest memories to a query, optionally within a cohort.

params.name: filter_col
params.desc: Column to restrict the cohort on (needs filter_val).

params.name: filter_val
params.desc: Keep rows whose filter_col equals this.

params.name: id_col
params.desc: The column to report as the id of each row (default id).

params.name: content_col
params.desc: Optional column to return as the content of each row.

tools.name: fractal_agent_recommend_diverse
tools.desc: Repulsion-diverse top-k recommendations, NO LLM step: enables session Diversify, then repulsion-aware top-k so re-searches avoid recently-rejected items. Returns [{item_id,score}]. SIDE EFFECT: leaves Diversify ON for this session; call fractal_diversify_disable when done.

params.name: id_col
params.desc: The column to report as the id of each row (default id).

tools.name: fractal_agent_regime_triage
tools.desc: General-purpose regime check on any series: DFA exponent and drift, then a written triage.

params.name: context
params.desc: Optional JSON object handed to the reasoner as context.

tools.name: fractal_agent_route_task
tools.desc: Route a task to the nearest capability under a token budget, with a written justification.

params.name: cap_table
params.desc: Table of capabilities, one embedding per row.

tools.name: fractal_agent_schedule_workload
tools.desc: Place a workload on the nearest node by capability vector, with a written justification and confidence.

params.name: context
params.desc: Optional JSON object handed to the reasoner as context.

tools.name: fractal_agent_track_anomaly
tools.desc: Track deviation check: nearest peer plus the DFA exponent of the heading series, with a written assessment.

params.name: id_col
params.desc: The column to report as the id of each row (default id).

tools.name: fractal_agent_trajectory_predict
tools.desc: Project the next state: the drift since a baseline row applied to the current state (rows). No model.

params.name: table_name
params.desc: Table with a single-column primary key.

params.name: forecast_steps
params.desc: Reserved for a future extrapolation step.

tools.name: fractal_audit_log
tools.desc: Append a record to the tamper-evident decision-audit chain. Needs the enterprise tier.

params.name: payload
params.desc: Payload, stored verbatim as a JSON document.

tools.name: fractal_audit_unpack
tools.desc: Decode a persisted audit blob (hex) into its JSON.

tools.name: fractal_change_point_detect
tools.desc: DFA's complement: localizes WHERE a series' mean and/or variance shifted, via a sliding two-sample test over adjacent windows. Returns {'indices':[...]}, ascending, up to max_points.

params.name: threshold
params.desc: Pooled-stddev units to flag a boundary.

tools.name: fractal_cortical_folding
tools.ret: STRUCT(mesh_area DOUBLE, hull_area DOUBLE, gyrification_index DOUBLE)
tools.desc: Gyrification Index (Zilles et al. 1988) from a pre-extracted brain-surface mesh. Returns {'mesh_area','hull_area','gyrification_index'}.

tools.name: fractal_cross_modal_search
tools.desc: Weighted concatenation of two modality vectors (e.g. morphology + clinical) before the search: [morphology*alpha, clinical*(1-alpha)]. Returns [{doc_id, distance}]; doc_id is a 0-indexed scan position, not a row locator.

params.name: alpha_weight
params.desc: Weight given to the morphology vector, in [0,1].

tools.name: fractal_cycle_detect
tools.desc: Find a cycle in a stream of fingerprints (Brent), tolerating a few differing bits (rows).

tools.name: fractal_detect_collapse
tools.desc: Current diversity quotient (D_q) for THIS session from the last search. Returns null when Diversify is off or nothing has searched yet.

tools.name: fractal_dimension_boxcount
tools.desc: Minkowski-Bouligand box-counting dimension of a point cloud. Documented minimum 8 points; for a STABLE estimate this org's own testing found it needs hundreds.

tools.name: fractal_dimension_dfa
tools.desc: DFA scaling exponent (alpha): ~0.5 uncorrelated noise, ~1.0 1/f pink noise, ~1.5 Brownian motion, <0.5 anti-correlated. Documented minimum 16 points; this org's own testing found ~24 is the real floor for a stable estimate.

tools.name: fractal_dimension_drift
tools.ret: STRUCT(drift DOUBLE, recent_alpha DOUBLE, baseline_alpha DOUBLE)
tools.desc: Regime-change detection: DFA exponent of the recent window vs the baseline. Returns {drift, recent_alpha, baseline_alpha}; drift is a SIGNED numeric (recent - baseline): positive = increasing complexity/irregularity, negative = approaching a more ordered state. Requires n >= window + 16, window >= 16.

tools.name: fractal_diversify_disable
tools.desc: Turns the Diversify/Repulsion layer back off for THIS session. fractal_agent_recommend_diverse leaves it ON; this is that tool's cleanup.

tools.name: fractal_diversify_enable
tools.desc: Turns on the stateful Diversify/Repulsion layer for THIS session: searches then avoid the neighbourhoods of negative-reported results ('shadows'). Off by default; session-scoped.

tools.name: fractal_diversify_set_params
tools.desc: Tunes the repulsion layer for THIS session. Every field optional; supplying only some keys keeps the core's current value for the rest. Takes effect on the next search.

tools.name: fractal_embed
tools.desc: Embed text with the configured embedding model; returns the vector.

tools.name: fractal_explain_result
tools.desc: Session-level Diversify diagnostics JSON: {dq, diversify_enabled, overhead_p99_us}.

tools.name: fractal_feedback_report
tools.desc: Reports dwell/positive/negative engagement on a prior search result, feeding the shadow store when Diversify is enabled. result_handle is the scan_pos the result came from, NOT its doc_id. kind must be 'dwell', 'positive' or 'negative'.

params.name: result_handle
params.desc: The scan_pos handle a prior search returned.

params.name: dwell_ms
params.desc: Dwell time in milliseconds (omit for a bare negative/positive).

tools.name: fractal_hybrid_clinical_search
tools.desc: Cohort-restricted sibling of fractal_search_telemetry: pass an explicit JSON array of rowid locators to restrict the scan before ranking. Errors 'doc_ids cohort matched no rows' on an empty cohort. doc_id/scan_pos semantics match fractal_search_telemetry, scan_pos counted within the cohort-filtered corpus.

params.name: doc_ids
params.desc: The cohort: rowid locators into table_name.

tools.name: fractal_isolate_background
tools.desc: Convenience wrapper for fractal_feedback_report(result_handle,'negative') with no dwell time: reject the result's neighbourhood outright.

params.name: result_handle
params.desc: The scan_pos handle to reject outright.

tools.name: fractal_ledger_compact
tools.desc: Compact the ledger. Needs the enterprise tier.

tools.name: fractal_ledger_flush
tools.desc: Persist the ledger to its file. Needs the enterprise tier.

tools.name: fractal_ledger_load
tools.desc: Load the persisted ledger into memory. Needs the enterprise tier.

tools.name: fractal_ledger_reset_hard
tools.desc: Erase the ledger entirely. Irreversible. Needs the enterprise tier.

tools.name: fractal_ledger_reset_soft
tools.desc: Clear the in-memory shadow state, keeping the truth ledger. Needs the enterprise tier.

tools.name: fractal_ledger_shadow_count
tools.desc: Entries in the shadow ledger. Needs the enterprise tier.

tools.name: fractal_ledger_truth_count
tools.desc: Entries in the truth ledger. Needs the enterprise tier.

tools.name: fractal_ledger_verify
tools.desc: Walks the ENTIRE chain for the given kind (O(n)). Returns {'ok':true,'rows_verified':N} or {'ok':false,'first_failure_id':ID,'reason':...}. Pure read-only forensic query; works even with NO enterprise library loaded, so a CISO audit never needs a license.

tools.name: fractal_morphological_complexity
tools.desc: Box-counting dimension + lacunarity of a pre-segmented mask. GOTCHA: wants ~256+ occupied points for a stable read; smaller clouds fail with rc=-1 rather than a confident wrong number. Returns {'dimension','lacunarity'}.

params.name: points
params.desc: Pre-segmented mask's occupied points (~256+ for a stable read).

tools.name: fractal_nerve_plexus_metric
tools.ret: STRUCT(fiber_length_density DOUBLE, branch_density DOUBLE, fractal_dimension DOUBLE)
tools.desc: Nerve-fiber plexus density + dimension from pre-extracted skeleton geometry (corneal confocal microscopy convention). Returns {'fiber_length_density','branch_density','fractal_dimension'}.

tools.name: fractal_optimize_portfolio_multimodal_pareto
tools.desc: Pareto-front sibling: same restarts, scored by decomposed (return,risk), NSGA-II crowding-distance truncated. Returns {'candidates':[{'return','risk','sharpe','weights'}],'n_found':N}. Enterprise tier.

tools.name: fractal_optimize_portfolio_multimodal
tools.desc: Multi-restart diverse-candidate sibling of fractal_optimize_portfolio. Returns {'candidates':[{'sharpe','weights'}],'n_found':N}. Enterprise tier: clean 'not loaded' error on Community.

params.name: use_obl
params.desc: Requires an enterprise core build with OBL support.

tools.name: fractal_optimize_portfolio
tools.desc: SFS cardinality-constrained Sharpe-ratio maximizer: the best K assets out of a large universe without brute-force exponential cost. Returns {'sharpe','weights'} (<=k nonzero, non-negative, summing to 1.0).

params.name: cov
params.desc: Flattened 1-D row-major n x n covariance.

params.name: use_obl
params.desc: Opposition-Based Learning per SFS trial (off by default; doubles the affected step's cost).

tools.name: fractal_optimize_subset
tools.desc: Value-weighted k-subset allocation over ANY scored item list: maximize sum(weight[i]*item_values[i]) with at most k nonzero, each weight<=upper_bounds[i], summing to 1.0. Returns {'score','weights'}. The sum of the k largest upper_bounds must reach 1.0 or no feasible subset exists (clean engine error).

tools.name: fractal_periodogram
tools.desc: Classical periodogram via exact O(n^2) DFT (not FFT). Returns {'freqs':[...], 'power':[...]}: top max_peaks bins, descending power. Catches network-beaconing/retry-cadence DFA alone misses.

tools.name: fractal_rag_agent
tools.desc: Retrieval-augmented answer over a table (rows: answer, source_row_ids, used_index, context_cut): embeds the question, retrieves (through a fractal_index when agent_use_index allows it), and answers from the hits. meta_filter, a flat JSON object of column: value pairs, limits the rows searched. Needs an embedding provider and a model.

params.name: meta_filter
params.desc: Flat JSON object of column: value pairs; only rows where every column equals its value are searched.

tools.name: fractal_reason
tools.desc: Send a question (and optional context) to the configured reasoning model. Needs a model endpoint; otherwise a clean not-configured error.

tools.name: fractal_schema_context
tools.desc: The schema (tables, columns, keys, comments) as text, for composing text-to-SQL questions. Read it before calling fractal_text_to_sql.

params.name: table_names
params.desc: Tables to scope to (list of names).

params.name: query_hint
params.desc: Optional hint to focus the schema context.

tools.name: fractal_search_agent
tools.desc: Embed a question, find the nearest rows of a table (a Scout search, or through a fractal_index when agent_use_index allows it), and answer from the hits (rows: answer, execution_time_ms, source_row_ids, used_index, context_cut). meta_filter limits the rows searched. Needs an embedding provider and a model.

params.name: meta_filter
params.desc: Flat JSON object of column: value pairs; only rows where every column equals its value are searched.

tools.name: fractal_sfs_converge_debug
tools.desc: Same Sniper convergence as fractal_sfs_converge with a full trajectory trace: {dim, generations, population_size, best_point, best_fit, best_fit_per_gen, paths}. best_point is a plain JSON array of numbers.

tools.name: fractal_search_explore
tools.desc: Scout-mode diverse population search: brute-force relevance scan over your embedding column followed by MMR re-ranking to prevent mode collapse; the anti-collapsed-top-K primitive.

params.name: options
params.desc: Optional JSON text of search options.

tools.name: fractal_sfs_converge
tools.desc: Raw Stochastic Fractal Search: the refined best point for a query, with no table. Use fractal_search_telemetry to search a table.

tools.name: fractal_search_telemetry
tools.desc: Ground-truth K-nearest real table rows to a query vector, by exact cosine distance: [{doc_id, distance, scan_pos}]. doc_id is the row's rowid (a real locator; resolve back with WHERE rowid = doc_id), or the row's 0-indexed position within the scan when the table has no rowid column; scan_pos is the 0-indexed position within THIS call's scan, the handle fractal_feedback_report/fractal_isolate_background want, distinct from doc_id.

tools.name: fractal_search_trajectory
tools.desc: Drift-vector search: finds the K nearest rows to (current_vector - baseline_vector) : 'what changed', not 'where am I'. Returns [{doc_id, distance}]. CAUTION: doc_id here is ALWAYS a 0-indexed scan position, never a row locator.

tools.name: fractal_spectrogram_entropy
tools.desc: Short-time spectral entropy: slides a window over a series and returns, per frame, the normalized Shannon entropy (0..1) of its power spectrum (mean removed, Hann tapered). Low = energy in a few frequencies (beacon, retry loop, locked carrier); high = spread across the band (noise, jamming, lost structure). A constant frame reports 0.0, never NaN. Returns {'entropy':[...]}, one value per frame; feed it to fractal_change_point_detect to localize WHEN the structure changed.

tools.name: fractal_sql_agent
tools.desc: Text-to-SQL with review and (only when auto_execute is true) execution of the generated statement under this connection.

params.name: auto_execute
params.desc: NEVER defaults to true: explicit opt-in to run the generated SQL under this connection's role.

tools.name: fractal_state_fingerprint
tools.desc: Random-hyperplane SimHash (Charikar 2002) of a state vector, returned as a hex string, (n_bits+7)/8 bytes. Near-identical states collapse to the same or low-Hamming-distance fingerprint. GOTCHA: encode scalar states one-hot, not 1-dim.

tools.name: fractal_tda_persistence_diagram
tools.ret: STRUCT(h0_bars STRUCT(birth DOUBLE, death DOUBLE)[], betti1 BIGINT)
tools.desc: Topological persistence over a point cloud's Vietoris-Rips filtration. Returns {'n_h0_bars':N,'h0_bars':[{birth,death}...],'betti1':N|null}. betti1 is the underlying GRAPH's cycle rank, NOT full simplicial H1 (over-counts when a filled triangle exists).

tools.name: fractal_text_to_sql
tools.desc: Generate one validated SELECT from a question. Never executes it.

params.name: table_names
params.desc: Tables to scope to (list of names).

tools.name: fractal_vascular_network
tools.ret: STRUCT(mean_tortuosity DOUBLE, branch_density DOUBLE, fractal_dimension DOUBLE)
tools.desc: Vessel-network tortuosity + branch-density + fractal dimension from PRE-EXTRACTED graph geometry (not raw imaging). Returns {'mean_tortuosity','branch_density','fractal_dimension'}.

tools.name: fractal_vector_hamming_distance
tools.desc: Hamming distance between two binary-quantized vectors (hex strings). A cheap pre-filter ahead of a full-precision re-rank, not a distance substitute.

tools.name: fractal_vectorizer_create
tools.desc: Register a vectorizer on a table column and backfill its queue with the rows that need embedding. Embedding itself happens in fractal_vectorizer_process_queue.

params.name: source_table
params.desc: Table to sync (needs a single-column primary key).

tools.name: fractal_vectorizer_drop
tools.desc: PERMANENT AND IRREVERSIBLE: deregisters the vectorizer, drops its trigger and deletes its config/queue history. For a temporary stop use pause instead.

tools.name: fractal_vectorizer_pause
tools.desc: Disables a vectorizer (idempotent). New writes aren't queued; the processor skips existing pending rows. Clean error on a nonexistent id.

tools.name: fractal_vectorizer_process_queue
tools.desc: Drives the actual embedding sync: call on your own schedule; there is NO background worker in any engine, by design. Runs in a single transaction; failed rows are NOT retried automatically.

tools.name: fractal_vectorizer_resume
tools.desc: Re-enables a paused vectorizer. Clean error on a nonexistent id.

tools.name: fractal_vectorizer_status
tools.desc: One row per vectorizer: its source, progress and failures.

tools.name: fractal_vector_lp_distance
tools.desc: Generalized L_p distance, any p > 0. For 0 < p < 1 this is NOT a proper metric; never substitute silently for cosine/L2.

tools.name: fractal_vector_quantize_binary
tools.desc: 1-bit (sign) quantization: 32x compression, (dim+7)/8 bytes, MSB-first, returned as a hex string. Pairs with fractal_vector_hamming_distance for cheap pre-filtering.

tools.name: fractal_vector_quantize_int8
tools.desc: Symmetric int8 quantization of one vector (4x compression). Returns {'scale':S,'codes':[...]}; dequantize via v[i] ~= codes[i]*scale.

tools.name: fractal_search
tools.desc: Approximate nearest neighbours from the native IVF index: [{doc_id, distance, scan_pos}]. The index proposes the candidates and every one of them is verified against the base table, so the distance reported is the exact double-precision cosine. With no index (or with use_index=false) it is an exact scan. Indexed search does NOT apply Diversify repulsion: use fractal_search_explore for a diverse population. The ids option restricts the search to a set of keys: a short set is scanned exactly, a long one goes through the index and is filtered.

params.name: options
params.desc: Search options: index, nprobe, rerank, use_index, verify, model. ids:int[] restricts the search to those keys (a short set is scanned exactly, a long one goes through the index and is filtered).

tools.name: fractal_index_candidates
tools.desc: The candidate row ids for Scout: every row of the nearest cells, plus a few representatives of every other cell, plus the rows committed after the index was built.

params.name: options
params.desc: Candidate options: near (cells in full), per_cell (representatives of the rest), index.

tools.name: fractal_index_create
tools.desc: Builds the native IVF index over a vector column and stores it in the database (fractal_index_meta / fractal_index_cells). The build streams: the corpus is never held in memory. The recall calibration chooses the nprobe.

params.name: options
params.desc: Index options: name, vector_format, nlist, pca_dim, iters, sample, seed, target_recall, calibration_samples, id_col.

tools.name: fractal_index_rebuild
tools.desc: Rebuilds an existing index from the current rows, keeping its options.

tools.name: fractal_index_drop
tools.desc: Drops an index and its stored cells.

tools.name: fractal_index_info
tools.desc: An index's format, sizes, staleness, recall calibration and the statistics of the last search (rows_scanned, cells_probed) -- the evidence that the index was used. Also a status (ready, stale, degraded, empty or orphaned) and an advice list: for example 'refresh: 60 rows were added since the build', 'rebuild: 30% of the rows were deleted', or 'the build's calibration reached recall 0.63 against a target of 0.95'.

tools.name: fractal_index_list
tools.desc: The catalog: one row per index with name, table_name, vector_col, format, dim, rows indexed, rows_now, stale, status (ready, stale, degraded, empty or orphaned) and generation. No rows means no index has been built in this database.

tools.name: fractal_index_refresh
tools.desc: Folds the rows added since the build into the index's cells, as a new generation switched in atomically, without retraining (the model is kept). Returns {name, added, rows, generation, refreshed}. Deleted rows and changed vectors are not touched: use fractal_index_rebuild when fractal_index_info advises a rebuild.

tools.name: fractal_index_ensure
tools.desc: Leaves the index on a table and column fit to use, in one call: builds it when missing (created), folds in the added rows when that is all that is needed (refreshed), rebuilds after more than a quarter of the rows were added or a fifth deleted (rebuilt), and otherwise changes nothing (unchanged). Returns {name, action, status, generation, rows}. For a setup script or a scheduled job; a search never builds or changes an index.

params.name: options
params.desc: Used only when it builds: the same options as fractal_index_create.

tools.name: fractal_chunk_text
tools.desc: Splits text into chunks of at most chunk_size characters (code points) and returns a JSON array of {no, start, end, text}; start and end are character offsets, end exclusive. chunk_mode paragraph (default) packs whole paragraphs, sentence packs whole sentences, fixed cuts every chunk_size - chunk_overlap characters; a paragraph or sentence longer than chunk_size is cut with chunk_overlap shared. Pure: no model, the same output on every FractalSQL host.

params.name: chunk_overlap
params.desc: Characters shared by neighbouring pieces when a paragraph or sentence has to be cut, 0..chunk_size-1.

tools.name: fractal_store_morphology
tools.desc: Upserts a feature vector against a doc_id in the generic per-item feature store (table fractalsql_feature_store, created on first use). The last write wins. Returns 'ok'.

tools.name: fractal_mine_topology_negatives
tools.desc: Brute-force k-NN (true Euclidean, ascending) over the fractal_store_morphology feature store. Returns [{'doc_id','distance'}], nearest first. A stored row whose dimension differs from the surrogate is skipped, not an error.

params.name: surrogate_vector
params.desc: Query vector into the feature store.

tools.name: fractal_vector_from_text
tools.desc: Builds the canonical vector from an array of numbers. This engine's vector is a plain list of floats, so the input is the array itself, not a text form.

tools.name: fractal_vector_to_json
tools.desc: Renders a vector as JSON: the array of numbers, so a client can see exactly what the engine holds.

tools.name: fractal_vector_dims
tools.desc: The vector's dimension: how many components it has. Check it before handing a vector to the vectorizer.

tools.name: fractal_vector_norm
tools.desc: The vector's L2 norm (its magnitude).

tools.name: fractal_vector_normalize
tools.desc: The vector scaled to unit length, so a distance between two vectors reflects direction only.

tools.name: fractal_vector_add
tools.desc: The element-wise sum of two vectors.

tools.name: fractal_vector_sub
tools.desc: The element-wise difference of two vectors.

tools.name: fractal_vector_l2_distance
tools.desc: The L2 (Euclidean) distance between two vectors.

tools.name: fractal_vector_l2_squared
tools.desc: The squared L2 distance: the same measure without the square root.

tools.name: fractal_vector_cosine_distance
tools.desc: The cosine distance between two vectors: 0 when they point the same way, 1 when they are orthogonal.

tools.name: fractal_vector_cosine_similarity
tools.desc: The cosine similarity between two vectors: 1 when they point the same way, 0 when they are orthogonal.

tools.name: fractal_vector_scale
tools.desc: The vector multiplied by a scalar factor.
